transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I, um… I’ve been having these thoughts while working on a memorial piece for my aunt. Like I might dishonor her somehow if I choose the wrong photo or color. It sounds small, but I can’t really shake it the way I usually can with creative doubts.
Do you find yourself needing a lot of reassurance or struggling with doubts like this in other parts of your life, or is it mainly when you’re working on this memorial?

It’s… mainly with the memorial, I think. I keep getting stuck on these thoughts that if I pick the wrong photo or color, it means I’m dishonoring my aunt somehow, or that I didn’t love her enough. I know that sounds extreme, but I can’t seem to just let it pass like I usually would.
Do you often feel anxious or distressed about making mistakes or not getting things exactly right in areas of your life outside of this memorial project?
I don’t think so… not often. I mean, I can be particular about my work, but this feels more… stuck than usual. Outside of this, I haven’t really noticed it being a big problem.
Outside of the memorial project, do you find yourself feeling anxious or distressed about things being just right in your daily life, like routines, work, or relationships?
Not really… I mean, I like things to look right, especially with art, but I don’t think my daily routines or relationships are usually like this. I haven’t noticed it much outside of the memorial.

Do you ever feel anxious or distressed about small details needing to be perfect in areas outside of your art or the memorial, like household items being arranged a certain way or how you complete daily tasks?
Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I might straighten something if it looks messy, but it doesn’t usually make me anxious or anything. I haven’t really noticed that outside of the art stuff.
Do these worries about the memorial photo and colors cause you a lot of anxiety or distress, even though you know they might not make sense?

Yes… it does. I know it probably doesn’t make sense, but it feels really upsetting in the moment. Like if I choose the wrong photo or the colors aren’t right, it somehow means I’m dishonoring my aunt, or that I didn’t love her enough. I can’t really just dismiss it like a normal art worry.

When you feel distressed about the photo or color choices for the memorial, do you find yourself doing something repeatedly, like checking, changing things back and forth, or seeking reassurance, to try to feel better or make sure it’s right?

Yeah… I do. I’ll reread the label text a lot, and move the same things on the table just a little, over and over. I keep checking photos of the layout too, until it feels… settled, I guess. Even though I know it’s probably already fine. It just eats up studio time.
How much time do these repeated checks and changes to the memorial layout take up in a day, and does it interfere with other things you need to do?

It depends on the day… sometimes it’s not huge, but it can take a while. I’m still getting most things done, mostly.

But… I did lose enough studio time that I missed a grant deadline. And I backed out of a gallery talk I’d wanted to do, because I just wasn’t ready. So, yeah, it’s interfering some.

Have you ever had similar thoughts or behaviors—like feeling stuck on certain ideas or needing to do things a certain way to feel reassured—in any other situations, even if they weren’t related to art or memorials?

Not really in the same way, no. This came up because of my aunt’s memorial piece. I just kept getting stuck on this thought that I might dishonor her somehow… like if I picked the wrong photo or color, it meant I didn’t love her enough. I knew that sounded extreme, but I couldn’t just let it go.
Outside of working on the memorial, do you ever have intrusive, unwanted thoughts that cause you significant anxiety or distress?

Not really outside of that. It’s mostly been with my aunt’s memorial piece… those thoughts about dishonoring her somehow, like if I chose the wrong photo or color it meant something awful about how much I loved her. I know that sounds… a lot, but I couldn’t just shake it.

Do these thoughts about the memorial and the need to keep checking or adjusting things ever make you feel so overwhelmed that you have trouble functioning normally, even outside the studio, like with sleep, relationships, or other responsibilities?

Not… completely, I guess. I’m still getting most of what I need to do done.

But it has cost me time in the studio. I missed a grant deadline because of it, and I backed out of a gallery talk I’d actually wanted to do. So… it’s not nothing.
